jobs.title: Product Engineer - Remote
jobs.description:
Overview 
Find the problem. Decide what to build. Ship it to production and prove it worked.
 Reporting to the CTO.
 Company Details 
Periskope helps businesses run customer conversations and operations on WhatsApp. Chats, groups, ticketing and automation live in one workspace, used by teams around the world.
 $2.5M+ ARR
 ~12 People
 Profitable · Global customers
 Seed · Saison Capital and Alliance
 Requirements
 2–5 years: In engineering, product, a founder's office, or your own startup.
 Product intuition: You can look at a screen and say what is wrong with it, and why.
 Proof you build: Something real you made with AI tools. A product, an internal tool, an automation people still use.
 Hustle: You unblock yourself. You do not wait for a spec, a designer or permission.
 Appetite for depth: You do not need to know production systems today. You need to want to own them.
 Clear communication: You explain decisions, flag uncertainty early, and move work forward in a remote team.
 Responsibilities
 Customer problems: Talk to users every week. Turn what you hear into a clear call on what to build next.
 Concept to production: Scope it, build it with agents, deploy it, and iterate on real usage.
 A product surface: Own a part of Periskope end to end, and the metric it moves.
 What ships: Challenge agent output, test assumptions, and stay accountable for the code and the result.
 Production reliability: When something breaks, find out why and fix it. Learn the data models, APIs and WhatsApp infrastructure underneath.
 Job Details
 Remote for candidates based in India.
 Interview Process 
Share your profile and one thing you took from idea to shipped: the problem, what you built, how you used agents, and what changed. Shortlisted candidates move through three steps.
 Conversation · Async on WhatsApp 
Talk through your work and product decisions with Bharat (CTO).
 Build together · 90 minutes 
Take a real Periskope problem from brief to working build, live with Bharat.
 Final conversation · 20 minutes 
Discuss the role and mutual fit with Swapnika (CEO).
 Why This Role Exists 
For years, building software needed two people. A PM decided what to build. An engineer wrote the code. Most of the time went into the handoff between them.
 That split no longer makes sense. AI agents now write most of our code. Typing code stopped being the bottleneck. Judgment took its place: knowing which problem matters, what the smallest useful fix is, and whether it holds up in production.
 A Product Engineer is one person doing the whole loop. You talk to the customer, make the call, direct the agents, ship the change and watch what happens next.
 How the Work Flows
 Listen: Sales calls, support chats, churn reasons, usage data.
 Decide: Pick the problem that matters. Cut it to the smallest useful fix.
 Build: Direct agents. Review every diff. Test what they assume.
 Ship: Release to real customers, behind a flag if it is risky.
 Measure: Check usage and tickets. Keep it, fix it or kill it.
 Then back to listening. A good loop takes days, not quarters.
 Who This Is For 
You do not need an engineering title. You need taste, speed, and a real wish to build things that run in production.
 Engineers: Who care more about the customer than the stack.
 Product managers: Who are tired of writing specs for someone else to build.
 Founder's office operators: Who already do a bit of everything and want to ship software too.
 Ex-founders: Who want to build product again, …

jobs.description:
About the role 
 We're building an agentic AI system that turns natural-language questions into accurate, governed answers over structured business data. This isn't a thin wrapper around a chat API — it's a multi-stage pipeline with retrieval, guardrails, and session state, and we need someone who can design and build that scaffolding, not just prompt a model well. You'll work on the reliability, safety, and scalability of an AI agent used in production by real customers.
 What you'll do 
 Design and build multi-step agent pipelines that combine LLM calls with deterministic logic — retrieval, validation, and business rules — rather than relying on a single prompt to do everything.
 Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): embedding-based search, ranking, and context assembly that stays within token/latency budgets as the underlying knowledge base grows.
 Build safeguards around model output — validating, sanitizing, and constraining what the AI is allowed to do or return before it reaches a user or a downstream system.
 Design for ambiguity: detect when a user's request is underspecified and decide whether to ask a clarifying question, apply a documented default, or refuse — rather than having the system silently guess.
 Own session and conversation state so multi-turn interactions stay coherent across follow-up questions.
 Write automated regression tests for AI-driven behavior, including "golden" test sets that catch quality regressions a human might not notice by eyeballing a few responses.
 Extend the system to new use cases/domains through configuration rather than one-off code, so growth doesn't multiply maintenance burden.
 Collaborate with frontend, data, and product stakeholders to ground the system in real business rules and correct data access boundaries.
 Instrument and monitor the pipeline in production — latency, cost, failure modes, and answer quality over time.
 Required qualifications

Software Engineer | Meridian Review Group
 Remote, London, Prague or Costa Rica | Full-Time or Long-Term Contract | $9,000–$12,000 per month depending on experience 
 Meridian Review Group is looking for a Software Engineer to join our growing international team and help build the technology behind a rapidly expanding network of independent business, markets and economic publications.
 This is a role for someone who wants to build, not simply maintain.
 Meridian currently operates specialist publications covering major economies, financial markets, companies, technology, investment and economic change. Our network includes Global Markets Review, British Business Review, American Commerce Review, German Business Review, Dutch Business Review, Czech Business Review and Gulf Business Review .
 We are building Meridian as much more than a collection of conventional news websites.
 Alongside journalism, we are developing market-data products, company and executive databases, rankings, economic datasets, research tools, structured entity systems, internal editorial technology and new ways for readers to understand companies, industries, markets and economies.
 The role can be fully remote or based from one of our locations in London, Prague or Costa Rica .
 What We’re Building
 Meridian Review Group is an international publishing, research and intelligence group covering business, markets, investment, technology, AI, energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, finance and economic policy.
 Our model combines timely journalism with information designed to remain useful long after publication.
 That includes:
 Company and executive profiles
 Market and stock data
 Economic and regional guides
 Industry directories
 Rankings and indexes
 Investment trackers
 Original research datasets
 Company, sector and geographic databases
 Searchable reference products
 Specialist newsletters and recurring editorial products
 Data-backed journalism
 Research and intelligence products for professional audiences
 The network is already reaching a meaningful audience, but we are building the infrastructure with a much larger goal in mind.
 Our ambition is to create a publishing and information platform capable of reaching millions of readers every month , ultimately building toward 10 million monthly visitors across the Meridian network . We currently reach approximately 480,000 readers across our publications in under a year and are growing rapidly.
 That creates a very different engineering challenge from building a single publication.
 We need systems that can support multiple brands, thousands and eventually hundreds of thousands of content and entity pages, rapidly growing search traffic, structured datasets, financial information, new publications and entirely new research products without the platform becoming increasingly difficult to maintain.
 We want to build systems that work well today while being designed for what Meridian could become several years from now.
 One Platform, Multiple Publications
 One of the more interesting parts of the engineering challenge is that Meridian is not one website.
 Much of the network operates from a shared technical foundation, while each publication maintains its own identity, editorial focus, domain, information architecture and audience.

jobs.description:
Vedika.io | Remote | Full-time
 CLAUDE MASTER. TOKEN MAXXING. Engineering judgment required.
 We’re building an AI-native company around APIs and personalized-advice software. We’re looking for an engineer who wants to understand the entire system: the data a model learns from, the evidence used to evaluate it, and the infrastructure that turns its output into a reliable product.
 You’ll contribute to technical work across LLM training and fine-tuning, evaluation, inference and agent workflows. The goal is measurable improvement, not a convincing demo that fails outside its happy path.
 WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON
 • Training data: curate examples, define annotation criteria, identify duplicates and leakage, and construct useful train, validation and test splits.
 • Model adaptation: help design fine-tuning experiments where appropriate; compare them against prompting and retrieval baselines before assuming training is necessary.
 • Evaluation: build representative test sets, error taxonomies and regression checks. Assess task accuracy, instruction-following and unsupported claims separately.
 • Inference: investigate latency, token usage and cost; test context selection, caching and model routing without silently sacrificing output quality.
 • Agent systems: develop tool-calling, MCP and computer-use workflows with validation, bounded permissions, retries and observable failure paths.
 • Product engineering: build APIs and integrations, write tests and deliver changes another engineer can reproduce, review and maintain.
 MANDATORY WORKING KNOWLEDGE
 • Python or TypeScript, REST APIs, SQL, Git and testing.
 • Claude Code and Codex: practical workflows for investigating, implementing and verifying changes.
 • Computer-use tools: browser or desktop workflows, outcome verification and approval boundaries.
 • Slack and Jira/Atlassian: clear communication, documented decisions and accurate task/blocker tracking.
 Familiarity with PyTorch, Hugging Face, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, Docker or cloud deployment is valuable. You are not expected to be an expert in every area. Strong fundamentals, careful experimentation and the ability to learn matter.
 HOW WE WANT TO WORK
 High ownership, fast feedback and substantive technical discussion. Question assumptions respectfully. Make uncertainty explicit. Share failures early. Leave evidence and documentation that help the next person move faster.
 ENTRY ROUTES
 Candidates with relevant experience will be considered directly for full-time employment. Candidates without relevant experience will start with a six-month internship, with a performance-based pre-placement offer (PPO) opportunity. A PPO is not automatic or guaranteed.
 Candidates from Tier 1 institutions are preferred. Strong applicants from other institutions are welcome and should demonstrate relevant ability through their work.
 APPLY WITH EVIDENCE
 Share a project, repository or experiment. Explain your contribution, baseline, evaluation method, failure cases and what the results actually support.
 Hiring urgently. Read the complete JD before applying. Apply only if you can meet the full-time commitment and demonstrate working knowledge of the mandatory tools. Include your relevant experience and earliest realistic joining date.
